title: AI Vendor Assessment Addendum
text:
AI Vendor Assessment Addendum (AIV-STD, Current)
Section: 1. Purpose and Applicability

## 1. Purpose and Applicability

This addendum supplements DUE-STD for vendors that supply artificial intelligence or machine-learning services to Northwind. It applies when a vendor's service generates content, makes or recommends decisions, classifies or scores data, or uses a model trained or fine-tuned by the vendor or a fourth party. It applies equally to an AI feature added to an existing product; the Vendor Manager must notify the TPRM Office within 10 business days of learning that an existing vendor has enabled such a feature.

title: AI Vendor Assessment Addendum

AI Vendor Assessment Addendum (AIV-STD, Current)
Section: 2. Minimum Tier

## 2. Minimum Tier

An AI vendor that processes Northwind Confidential data or personal data is Tier 2 at minimum. An AI vendor whose output is used in a decision about a client, such as credit, onboarding, fraud, or suitability, is Tier 1, regardless of spend.

AI Vendor Assessment Addendum (AIV-STD, Current)
Section: 4. Use of Northwind Data for Training

## 4. Use of Northwind Data for Training

Using Northwind data, including prompts, inputs, outputs, and feedback, to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve the vendor's models or any third party's models is prohibited without prior written consent from the Northwind Data Owner and Legal. The prohibition must be written into the contract and the DPA (DPA-REQ clause 10). Consent, where given, must name the data set and purpose and may be withdrawn on 30 days' notice.

Fully automated decisions affecting clients require approval from the Chief Data and AI Officer and Legal.

## 6. Evaluation Evidence

Tier 1 and Tier 2 AI vendors provide evaluation evidence at onboarding and at least annually thereafter. Evidence must cover accuracy or quality metrics for Northwind's use case, bias and fairness testing across relevant groups, robustness testing including prompt-injection resistance for generative systems, and the results of red-team exercises. The Chief Data and AI Officer's team reviews this evidence alongside the CISO office's security review.

## 7. Harmful Output Incidents

The vendor must notify Northwind within 72 hours of becoming aware of harmful or materially incorrect output affecting Northwind, as set out in INCN-SLA. Harmful output includes discriminatory output, disclosure of another customer's data, fabricated facts presented as fact in a regulated communication, and output generated through a successful prompt-injection attack. Northwind employees who observe harmful output report it to the TPRM Office the same business day.

title: Cloud Service Provider Assessment Standard
text:
Cloud Service Provider Assessment Standard (CLD-STD, Current)
Section: 1. Purpose

## 1. Purpose

Cloud service providers (CSPs) change the shape of third-party risk. Northwind shares responsibility for security with the provider, data may move across regions, and many vendors depend on the same few platforms. This standard adds cloud-specific requirements on top of DUE-STD. It applies to infrastructure, platform, and software-as-a-service providers that store or process Northwind data.

title: Cloud Service Provider Assessment Standard
text:
Cloud Service Provider Assessment Standard (CLD-STD, Current)
Section: 2. Tiering

## 2. Tiering

A CSP that hosts Restricted data or supports a critical business service is Tier 1 under TIER-MTX regardless of spend. A SaaS provider hosted on a CSP is assessed as a vendor in its own right; its CSP is a fourth party (FRTH-POL).

title: Cloud Service Provider Assessment Standard
text:
Cloud Service Provider Assessment Standard (CLD-STD, Current)
Section: 3. Assurance

## 3. Assurance

3.1 Tier 1 and Tier 2 CSPs provide a SOC 2 Type II report meeting DUE-STD §4.2. CSA STAR Level 2 certification is accepted as an alternative for Tier 2 CSPs with CISO office approval.

3.2 The CSP must publish, or provide under NDA, a shared responsibility matrix. The CISO office maps every control in the matrix marked as a customer responsibility to a Northwind control owner before go-live.

title: Cloud Service Provider Assessment Standard
text:
Cloud Service Provider Assessment Standard (CLD-STD, Current)
Section: 4. Data Location

## 4. Data Location

4.1 Northwind data may be stored only in the approved regions: United States, European Union, and United Kingdom.

4.2 Storing data, or replicating backups, in any other region requires approval from the CISO office and Legal, and a DPA amendment where personal data is involved (DPA-REQ §3).

4.3 The CSP contract must require at least 90 days' notice of any change to the regions in which Northwind data is stored.

title: Cloud Service Provider Assessment Standard
text:
Cloud Service Provider Assessment Standard (CLD-STD, Current)
Section: 5. Encryption and Keys

## 5. Encryption and Keys

5.1 All Northwind data must be encrypted in transit with TLS 1.2 or higher and at rest with AES-256 or equivalent.

5.2 Restricted data must be encrypted with customer-managed keys held in a Northwind-controlled key management service or hardware security module. The CSP must not have the ability to access customer-managed keys in plaintext.

5.3 Customer-managed keys are rotated at least every 12 months.

Cloud Service Provider Assessment Standard (CLD-STD, Current)

Administrative access to Northwind tenants uses Northwind's identity provider with MFA (ACC-STD). The CSP must make audit logs for Northwind tenants available for export to Northwind's security monitoring platform, with at least 12 months of log history retrievable.

7.2 The exit plan (EXIT-PLN) must show that data can be exported in a non-proprietary format and describe how workloads would be rebuilt on an alternative platform.

title: Concentration Risk Standard
text:
Concentration Risk Standard (CONC-STD, Current)
Section: 1. Purpose

## 1. Purpose

Individually sound vendor relationships can add up to an unsound portfolio. When too many services depend on one vendor, one region, or one underlying technology, a single failure can disrupt several critical business services at once. This standard sets the thresholds Northwind monitors and what happens when one is crossed.

title: Concentration Risk Standard
text:
Concentration Risk Standard (CONC-STD, Current)
Section: 2. Types of Concentration

## 2. Types of Concentration

- **Vendor concentration** — dependence on a single vendor, including its affiliates, across many contracts.
- **Service concentration** — multiple critical business services relying on the same vendor.
- **Geographic concentration** — Tier 1 vendors delivering from the same country or metropolitan area, exposed to the same natural disaster, political, or infrastructure event.
- **Fourth-party concentration** — many vendors depending on the same subcontractor, most commonly the same cloud service provider (FRTH-POL, CLD-STD).
- **Substitutability** — services for which no alternative provider could be onboarded within 12 months.

title: Concentration Risk Standard
text:
Concentration Risk Standard (CONC-STD, Current)
Section: 3. Thresholds

## 3. Thresholds

The TPRM Office flags a concentration when any of these are met:

1. A single vendor group accounts for more than 15% of Northwind's total annual third-party spend.
2. A single vendor supports more than 3 critical business services.
3. More than 40% of Tier 1 vendors deliver primarily from the same country, excluding the United States.
4. A single fourth party supports more than 5 Tier 1 vendors.
5. A Tier 1 service is rated non-substitutable and has no tested exit plan under EXIT-PLN.

title: Concentration Risk Standard
Concentration Risk Standard
text:
Concentration Risk Standard (CONC-STD, Current)
Section: 5. Response to a Flag

## 5. Response to a Flag

A flag does not prohibit the engagement. It requires a decision. The Business Owner and the TPRM Office prepare a concentration memo stating the business rationale, the mitigations, and the residual risk. Mitigations may include a secondary provider, multi-region deployment, strengthened exit planning, or contractual step-in rights. The memo is approved by the TPRC. A threshold 2 or threshold 5 flag also requires Chief Risk Officer approval.

title: Concentration Risk Standard
text:
Concentration Risk Standard (CONC-STD, Current)
Section: 6. Reporting

## 6. Reporting

The TPRM Office produces a quarterly concentration report for the TPRC covering all five thresholds, trends against the prior four quarters, and the status of approved mitigations. The report also lists the top 10 vendors by spend and the top 10 fourth parties by number of dependent Tier 1 vendors.

title: Concentration Risk Standard
text:
Concentration Risk Standard (CONC-STD, Current)
Section: 7. Data Sources

## 7. Data Sources

The report draws on the vendor inventory, the Business Impact Register, Accounts Payable spend data, and the fourth-party inventory maintained under FRTH-POL. Vendor Managers must keep the critical-service mapping in ProcureNet current; an inaccurate mapping is the most common cause of a missed concentration flag.

Contract Renewal Procedure (RNW-PRC, Current)
Section: Section 1 — Purpose

## Section 1 — Purpose

A renewal is a fresh decision to continue a relationship, not an administrative formality. This procedure ensures the decision is taken with current risk and performance information and with enough time to exit or re-source if the answer is no.

title: Contract Renewal Procedure
text:
Contract Renewal Procedure (RNW-PRC, Current)
Section: Section 2 — Renewal Notice Windows

## Section 2 — Renewal Notice Windows

The Vendor Manager must open a renewal case in ProcureNet no later than the following number of days before the contract expiry date:

| Tier | Renewal case opened |
|---|---|
| Tier 1 | 120 days before expiry |
| Tier 2 | 90 days before expiry |
| Tier 3 | 60 days before expiry |
| Tier 4 | 30 days before expiry |

ProcureNet sends reminders 30 days before each window opens. A renewal case opened late must be reported to the Head of Procurement, and a Tier 1 or Tier 2 case opened late is also reported to the TPRC.

title: Contract Renewal Procedure
text:
Contract Renewal Procedure (RNW-PRC, Current)
Section: Section 3 — Renewal Risk Review

## Section 3 — Renewal Risk Review

Before any renewal is approved, the Vendor Manager completes a renewal risk review covering:

1. Reassessment status. If the vendor's next reassessment under DUE-STD §5 falls due within 6 months of the renewal date, the reassessment is performed now as part of the renewal. An overdue reassessment blocks renewal.
2. Performance. The last four performance scorecards under PERF-STD, including any open performance improvement plan.
3. Open findings and exceptions. All open DUE-STD findings and EXC-PRC exceptions, with their expiry dates.
4. Incidents. Any incident notified under INCN-SLA during the term, and whether notification deadlines were met.
5. Scope change. Any change to data accessed, services supported, or spend that would change the tier under TIER-MTX.
6. Subcontractors. Any change to material subcontractors under FRTH-POL.
7. Concentration. For Tier 1 vendors, the TPRM Office confirms the renewal does not breach a threshold in CONC-STD.

title: Contract Renewal Procedure
text:
Contract Renewal Procedure (RNW-PRC, Current)
Section: Section 4 — Re-Sourcing

## Section 4 — Re-Sourcing

A renewal that increases total contract value above $250,000, where the original award was below that amount, must be competitively re-sourced under PRC-POL unless a sole-source justification is approved.

title: Contract Renewal Procedure
text:
Contract Renewal Procedure (RNW-PRC, Current)
Section: Section 5 — Auto-Renewal

## Section 5 — Auto-Renewal

5.1 Automatic renewal clauses are prohibited in Tier 1 and Tier 2 contracts. Every Tier 1 and Tier 2 renewal requires an affirmative decision recorded in ProcureNet.

5.2 Tier 3 and Tier 4 contracts may auto-renew only if the contract (a) limits each renewal term to 12 months or less and (b) allows Northwind to terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice.

5.3 Where an inherited contract contains a non-compliant auto-renewal clause, Legal must issue a non-renewal notice before the clause's notice deadline and the contract must be renegotiated.

text:
Contract Renewal Procedure (RNW-PRC, Current)

The Business Owner approves the renewal. Where the renewal risk review identifies a Critical or High finding without an approved exception, the renewal may not be approved. If the decision is not to renew, the Vendor Manager invokes the exit plan under EXIT-PLN at least 60 days before expiry for Tier 1 and Tier 2 vendors. Renewal records are retained with the contract under RET-SCH.

title: Data Processing Agreement Requirements
text:
Data Processing Agreement Requirements (DPA-REQ, Current)
Section: 1. When a DPA Is Required

## 1. When a DPA Is Required

A Data Processing Agreement (DPA) is required before any personal data is shared with a vendor, in any volume, including test or pilot data. "Personal data" means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person, including client, employee, and prospect data. Pseudonymized data is still personal data. Fully anonymized aggregate data is not, but the Privacy Office must confirm the anonymization method in writing.

A missing DPA cannot be covered by an exception under EXC-PRC. If personal data is involved, the DPA is mandatory.

title: Data Processing Agreement Requirements
text:
Data Processing Agreement Requirements (DPA-REQ, Current)
Section: 2. Mandatory Clauses

## 2. Mandatory Clauses

Legal uses the Northwind DPA template. Vendor paper is accepted only if it contains every clause below:

1. Processing only on Northwind's documented instructions, with the subject matter, duration, nature, purpose, data categories, and data subject categories listed in an annex.
2. Confidentiality commitments binding every person authorized to process the data.
3. Security measures at least equivalent to those evidenced during due diligence (DUE-STD §4).
4. Sub-processor controls: no new sub-processor without 30 days' prior written notice to Northwind and a right to object. Sub-processors are fourth parties and are also governed by FRTH-POL.
5. Assistance with data subject rights requests, with a response to Northwind within 5 business days of a request.
6. Breach notification within the deadlines in INCN-SLA, and in any case no later than 72 hours after the vendor becomes aware of a personal-data breach.
7. Assistance with data protection impact assessments and regulator consultations.
8. Deletion or return of all personal data at the end of the services, with certification, as set out in EXIT-PLN §4.2.
9. Audit and inspection rights consistent with AUDT-GDE.
10. A prohibition on using Northwind personal data to train, fine-tune, or improve the vendor's products or models without Northwind's written consent (see AIV-STD).
11. Liability for sub-processor failures as if they were the vendor's own.

## 3. International Transfers

Personal data may not be transferred or made accessible outside the jurisdiction in which it was collected without Legal approval. Transfers out of the EU, EEA, or UK require an approved transfer mechanism, normally the Standard Contractual Clauses or the UK International Data Transfer Addendum, plus a transfer impact assessment completed by Privacy Counsel. Remote access from another country counts as a transfer.

title: Fourth-Party (Subcontractor) Policy
text:
Fourth-Party (Subcontractor) Policy (FRTH-POL, Current)
Section: 1. Purpose

## 1. Purpose

Our vendors' vendors are our risk too. When a vendor subcontracts part of a service, Northwind data and Northwind services may depend on a party with which Northwind has no contract. This policy defines how those fourth parties are disclosed, approved, and monitored.

title: Fourth-Party (Subcontractor) Policy
text:
Fourth-Party (Subcontractor) Policy (FRTH-POL, Current)
Section: 2. Definitions

## 2. Definitions

- **Fourth party** — any subcontractor, sub-processor, or supplier used by a Northwind vendor in delivering services to Northwind.
- **Material subcontractor** — a fourth party that (a) stores, processes, or can access Northwind Confidential or Restricted data or personal data; (b) performs a part of the service whose failure would disrupt a critical or important business service; or (c) hosts the vendor's production environment.

title: Fourth-Party (Subcontractor) Policy
text:
Fourth-Party (Subcontractor) Policy (FRTH-POL, Current)
Section: 3. Disclosure

## 3. Disclosure

3.1 Tier 1 and Tier 2 vendors must disclose all material subcontractors during due diligence, including name, location, services performed, and data accessed.

3.2 Tier 1 vendors must give Northwind at least 60 days' prior written notice before adding or replacing a material subcontractor. Tier 2 vendors must give at least 30 days' notice, which aligns with the sub-processor notice period in DPA-REQ.

3.3 Northwind may object to a new material subcontractor. If the objection cannot be resolved, Northwind may terminate the affected services without penalty.

title: Fourth-Party (Subcontractor) Policy
text:

## 4. Approval

4.1 The TPRM Office assesses each new material subcontractor of a Tier 1 or Tier 2 vendor. The assessment covers security posture, location, sanctions screening (SANC-PRC), and concentration (CONC-STD).

4.2 Offshore subcontracting, meaning any material subcontractor performing services or accessing data outside the country in which the contracted vendor operates, requires approval from both the TPRM Office and Legal.

4.3 A new material subcontractor triggers an early reassessment of the vendor under TIER-MTX §3.

Procurement Policy (PRC-POL, Current)
Section: 1. Purpose

## 1. Purpose

This policy ensures Northwind buys goods and services fairly, at a defensible price, and with the right approvals. It works alongside TPR-POL: procurement decides how we choose a vendor, TPRM decides whether the chosen vendor is safe to use.

Right-to-Audit Clause Guide (AUDT-GDE, Current)
Section: Section 1 — Why This Matters

## Section 1 — Why This Matters

Northwind's regulators expect us to be able to examine how our outsourced services are actually run, not just what the vendor says about them. A right-to-audit clause is how we keep that ability after signature. This guide explains what the clause must contain and which concessions negotiators can and cannot make.

title: Right-to-Audit Clause Guide
section: Section 2 — When the Clause Is Required
text:
Right-to-Audit Clause Guide (AUDT-GDE, Current)
Section: Section 2 — When the Clause Is Required

## Section 2 — When the Clause Is Required

A right-to-audit clause is required in every Tier 1 and Tier 2 contract. It is recommended for Tier 3 contracts and is not required for Tier 4 (TIER-MTX §4).

title: Right-to-Audit Clause Guide
text:
Right-to-Audit Clause Guide (AUDT-GDE, Current)
Section: Section 3 — Required Elements

## Section 3 — Required Elements

The clause must give Northwind, its internal audit function, its external auditors, and its regulators the right to:

- inspect premises, systems, records, and personnel involved in delivering the services;
- obtain copies of policies, procedures, and evidence of control operation;
- extend these rights to material subcontractors (FRTH-POL).

title: Right-to-Audit Clause Guide
text:
Right-to-Audit Clause Guide (AUDT-GDE, Current)
Section: 3.1 Notice

### 3.1 Notice

Routine audits may require up to 30 days' prior written notice. For-cause audits, triggered by a security incident, a regulatory request, or a suspected material breach of contract, may require no more than 10 business days' notice.

title: Right-to-Audit Clause Guide
text:
Right-to-Audit Clause Guide (AUDT-GDE, Current)
Section: 3.2 Frequency

### 3.2 Frequency

The vendor may limit routine audits to once per 12-month period. For-cause audits and regulator audits may not be limited in number.

title: Right-to-Audit Clause Guide
text:
Right-to-Audit Clause Guide (AUDT-GDE, Current)
Section: 3.3 Regulator Access

### 3.3 Regulator Access

Regulator access must be unconditional. The clause may not require regulators to give notice, sign confidentiality agreements with the vendor, or bear the vendor's costs. Do not accept any wording that makes regulator access subject to the vendor's consent.

title: Right-to-Audit Clause Guide
text:
Right-to-Audit Clause Guide (AUDT-GDE, Current)
Section: 3.4 Cost

### 3.4 Cost

Each party bears its own costs for routine audits. The vendor bears the cost of a for-cause audit that confirms a material breach.

title: Right-to-Audit Clause Guide
text:
Right-to-Audit Clause Guide (AUDT-GDE, Current)
Section: Section 4 — Negotiation Positions

## Section 4 — Negotiation Positions

Vendors with many clients often resist individual audits. Acceptable concessions:

- **Pooled audits.** Northwind may join a pooled audit with other clients in place of an individual routine audit.
- **Reliance on assurance reports.** A current SOC 2 Type II report meeting DUE-STD §4.2 may satisfy a routine audit for the controls in its scope. The clause must keep Northwind's right to audit controls outside the report's scope.
- **Remote audits.** Routine audits may be conducted remotely by default, with on-site access reserved for for-cause audits.

Concessions that are never acceptable: removing regulator access, removing for-cause audits, limiting audits to the vendor's own selection of records, or requiring Northwind to pay for the vendor's staff time on a routine audit beyond 3 days.

Any deviation from Section 3 not listed as an acceptable concession requires an exception under EXC-PRC.

title: Right-to-Audit Clause Guide
text:
Right-to-Audit Clause Guide (AUDT-GDE, Current)
Section: Section 5 — Exercising the Right

## Section 5 — Exercising the Right

The Vendor Manager coordinates audit requests with Internal Audit and the TPRM Office. Audit findings are tracked as due diligence findings under DUE-STD §6.

Section: Section 5 — Adverse Media

## Section 5 — Adverse Media

Adverse media screening covers financial crime, fraud, bribery and corruption, sanctions evasion, human-rights abuse, and serious regulatory enforcement. It is performed at onboarding for Tier 1 and Tier 2 vendors and repeated annually for those tiers. Tier 3 and Tier 4 vendors receive sanctions screening only, unless a Business Owner or the TPRM Office requests adverse media screening.

title: Sanctions and Adverse Media Screening Procedure
text:

Section: Section 6 — Match Handling

## Section 6 — Match Handling

6.1 The screening tool generates alerts. Procurement Operations performs first-level review and closes clear false positives, recording the reason.

6.2 Any alert not closed as a false positive must be triaged by Financial Crimes Compliance (FCC) within 2 business days.

6.3 If FCC confirms a true match, it escalates to the Chief Compliance Officer and Legal within 24 hours. All payments to the vendor are blocked immediately, and the vendor master record is placed on hold.

6.4 Northwind staff must not tell the vendor why payments are held. Disclosure may breach sanctions or anti-tipping-off obligations; all communication goes through Legal.

6.5 A confirmed true match cannot be covered by an exception under EXC-PRC. The TPRM Office assesses invoking the stressed exit plan (EXIT-PLN §5).

Third-Party Risk Management Policy (TPR-POL, Current)
Section: 1. Purpose

## 1. Purpose

This policy establishes how Northwind Capital Group identifies, assesses, contracts with, monitors, and exits third parties. Regulators hold Northwind accountable for activities performed on its behalf, so outsourcing a service never outsources the risk. This policy is the master document for Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM); the standards and procedures it references set the detailed requirements.

title: Third-Party Risk Management Policy
text:
Third-Party Risk Management Policy (TPR-POL, Current)
Section: 2. Scope

## 2. Scope

This policy applies to every employee, contractor, and business unit that engages a third party. A third party is any external entity that provides goods or services to Northwind, receives Northwind data, connects to Northwind systems, or acts on Northwind's behalf with clients or regulators. This includes software-as-a-service providers, consultants, data brokers, outsourced operations, cloud service providers, and AI service providers. Intra-group affiliates are in scope where they provide services under an intercompany agreement.

Out of scope: utilities, government agencies acting in a regulatory capacity, and payments to individuals for employee reimbursements.

title: Third-Party Risk Management Policy
text:
Third-Party Risk Management Policy (TPR-POL, Current)
Section: 3. Roles and Responsibilities

## 3. Roles and Responsibilities

- **Business Owner** — the senior employee accountable for the relationship. Initiates the engagement, owns the risk, and funds remediation.
- **Vendor Manager** — manages the relationship day to day, runs performance reviews (PERF-STD), and recertifies vendor access (ACC-STD).
- **TPRM Office** — assigns the risk tier (TIER-MTX), coordinates due diligence (DUE-STD), maintains the third-party inventory, and administers exceptions (EXC-PRC).
- **Procurement** — runs sourcing and competitive bidding (PRC-POL) and creates the vendor master record (ONB-PRC).
- **CISO office** — performs information security and cloud assessments (DUE-STD, CLD-STD).
- **Legal** — negotiates contract terms, including data processing (DPA-REQ) and audit rights (AUDT-GDE).
- **Financial Crimes Compliance (FCC)** — adjudicates sanctions and adverse media matches (SANC-PRC).

Section: 3. Internal AI Assistant Interaction Logs

## 3. Internal AI Assistant Interaction Logs

Northwind employees use internal AI assistants to search and summarize TPRM policies and vendor files. Logs of these interactions are records under this schedule and are subject to the following rules:

3.1 Raw user prompts and raw assistant responses that contain personal data must not be stored for more than 30 days. The 30-day limit applies to all storage locations, including application logs, observability and tracing platforms, and debugging exports.

3.2 After 30 days, interaction logs may be kept only in summarized or hashed form. Summarized form means a record of the interaction metadata (timestamp, user identifier, documents retrieved, response latency, and evaluation scores) with personal data removed. Hashed form means prompts replaced by a one-way hash sufficient to detect duplicates but not to reconstruct the text.

3.3 Summarized or hashed logs are retained for up to 13 months from the date of interaction and then deleted automatically.

3.4 Logs subject to a legal hold are exempt from 3.1 to 3.3 for the duration of the hold, under the control of Legal.

3.5 System owners must document how their assistant meets 3.1 to 3.3 before production launch. The Records Management Office reviews this documentation annually.

Vendor Access Management Standard (ACC-STD, Current)

## 2. Scope

## 3. Preconditions

title: Vendor Access Management Standard
text:
Vendor Access Management Standard (ACC-STD, Current)
Section: 4. Requirements

## 4. Requirements

title: Vendor Access Management Standard
text:
Vendor Access Management Standard (ACC-STD, Current)
Section: 4. Requirements

1. Every vendor user has a named account tied to one identified individual. Shared, generic, or team accounts are prohibited.
2. Vendor accounts use the "v-" prefix and are created in the dedicated vendor directory, separate from employee accounts.
3. Multi-factor authentication is required for all vendor access, without exception, including access from vendor premises.
4. Remote access is permitted only through the Northwind vendor access gateway. Direct VPN connections from vendor networks require CISO office approval.
5. Access is granted on least privilege, limited to the systems and data named in the access request.
6. Every vendor account has an expiry date no later than 12 months from creation or the contract end date, whichever is earlier.
7. Privileged access is granted only through the privileged access management (PAM) system, is time-limited to the approved change window, and is session-recorded.
8. Session recordings for privileged vendor sessions are retained for 12 months.
9. Service accounts used by vendor systems are owned by a named Northwind employee, use vaulted credentials, and have credentials rotated at least every 90 days.
10. API keys issued to vendors are scoped to the minimum required endpoints and rotated at least every 90 days.
11. Accounts inactive for 30 days are disabled automatically.
12. Vendor personnel must complete Northwind security awareness training before access is enabled and annually thereafter.
13. Vendor access to production data from outside the approved regions in CLD-STD §4.1 requires CISO office and Legal approval.
14. Physical badges for vendor personnel are issued for no more than 90 days at a time and are returned on the last day on site.

title: Vendor Business Continuity and Resilience Requirements
text:
Vendor Business Continuity and Resilience Requirements (BCP-REQ, Current)
Section: Section 1 — Purpose

## Section 1 — Purpose

Northwind's own recovery commitments to clients and regulators are only as strong as the vendors behind them. This document sets the minimum business continuity and disaster recovery requirements vendors must meet, by tier.

title: Vendor Business Continuity and Resilience Requirements
text:
Vendor Business Continuity and Resilience Requirements (BCP-REQ, Current)
Section: Section 2 — Recovery Objectives

## Section 2 — Recovery Objectives

The recovery time objective (RTO) is the maximum time from service disruption to restoration. The recovery point objective (RPO) is the maximum period of data loss measured back from the moment of disruption.

| Tier | RTO | RPO | Plan testing | Test results to Northwind |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tier 1 | 4 hours | 15 minutes | Annually, full failover test | Within 30 days of the test |
| Tier 2 | 24 hours | 4 hours | Every 24 months | Within 30 days of the test |
| Tier 3 | 72 hours | 24 hours | Self-attestation at reassessment | On request |
| Tier 4 | Best effort | Best effort | Not required | Not required |

Where a vendor supports a critical business service with a stricter impact tolerance in the Business Impact Register, the stricter value applies and must be written into the contract.

title: Vendor Business Continuity and Resilience Requirements
Vendor Business Continuity and Resilience Requirements
text:
Vendor Business Continuity and Resilience Requirements (BCP-REQ, Current)
Section: Section 4 — Recovery Sites

## Section 4 — Recovery Sites

Tier 1 vendors must operate a recovery site, or a cloud region, at least 100 miles from the primary site and not dependent on the same power grid. Cloud-hosted Tier 1 services must also meet the multi-availability-zone requirement in CLD-STD §7.1.

title: Vendor Business Continuity and Resilience Requirements
text:
Vendor Business Continuity and Resilience Requirements (BCP-REQ, Current)
Section: Section 5 — Testing

## Section 5 — Testing

5.1 Tier 1 vendors perform a full failover test annually. Tabletop exercises do not satisfy this requirement.

5.2 Test reports must show the RTO and RPO actually achieved, issues found, and remediation dates.

5.3 Northwind may participate in or observe any test. For Tier 1 vendors supporting a critical business service, the Operational Resilience Office joins at least one test every 24 months.

5.4 A test that fails to meet the RTO or RPO is treated as a High finding under DUE-STD §6.

title: Vendor Exit and Offboarding Standard
text:
Vendor Exit and Offboarding Standard (EXIT-PLN, Current)
Section: 1. Purpose

## 1. Purpose

Every relationship ends. This standard ensures that when one does, whether planned or forced, Northwind gets its data back, removes the vendor's access promptly, and keeps its services running. It implements TPR-POL §4.5.

title: Vendor Exit and Offboarding Standard
text:
Vendor Exit and Offboarding Standard (EXIT-PLN, Current)
Section: 2. Exit Plans

## 2. Exit Plans

2.1 An exit plan is required for every Tier 1 and Tier 2 vendor. It is drafted by the Vendor Manager during onboarding and attached to the contract as a schedule before signature (ONB-PRC Step 5).

2.2 The exit plan must cover two scenarios:

- **Planned exit** — non-renewal or termination for convenience, with a transition period agreed in the contract.
- **Stressed exit** — the vendor fails suddenly through insolvency, a sanctions designation, a severe security incident, or a regulatory order. The plan must state how the service is maintained with no transition assistance from the vendor.

2.3 Each plan names the replacement option (alternate vendor, in-house capability, or orderly service discontinuation), the data to be returned and its format, the estimated transition time, and the cost estimate.

2.4 Tier 1 exit plans are tested by tabletop exercise every 24 months and reviewed at each annual reassessment. Tier 2 exit plans are reviewed at each reassessment.

A vendor that cannot pay its own bills cannot reliably deliver services to Northwind. This standard defines when and how vendor financial health is reviewed and what Northwind does when a vendor's position deteriorates.

title: Gifts, Entertainment and Vendor Conflicts of Interest Policy
text:
Gifts, Entertainment and Vendor Conflicts of Interest Policy (GIFT-POL, Current)
Section: Purpose

**Purpose.** Vendor decisions at Northwind must be made on merit. Gifts, hospitality, and personal relationships can influence those decisions, or appear to. This policy sets the limits for employees who select, manage, or approve payments to vendors, and for any employee who receives gifts or entertainment from a current or prospective vendor.

title: Gifts, Entertainment and Vendor Conflicts of Interest Policy
text:
Gifts, Entertainment and Vendor Conflicts of Interest Policy (GIFT-POL, Current)
Section: Scope

**Scope.** All Northwind employees and contractors. The policy covers gifts and entertainment offered by any current vendor, any prospective vendor, and any vendor's agent or subcontractor.

title: Gifts, Entertainment and Vendor Conflicts of Interest Policy
text:
Gifts, Entertainment and Vendor Conflicts of Interest Policy (GIFT-POL, Current)
Section: Gifts

**Gifts.** An employee may accept a gift from a vendor only if its value is $100 or less. The aggregate value of gifts accepted from any one vendor may not exceed $250 per calendar year per employee. Gifts above these limits must be politely declined or, if refusal would cause offense, surrendered to Compliance within 5 business days. Cash and cash equivalents, including gift cards, prepaid cards, vouchers, and securities, are prohibited at any value.

title: Gifts, Entertainment and Vendor Conflicts of Interest Policy
text:
Gifts, Entertainment and Vendor Conflicts of Interest Policy (GIFT-POL, Current)
Section: Entertainment

**Entertainment.** Business meals and events attended together with the vendor are entertainment, not gifts. Entertainment of up to $250 per person per event may be accepted without pre-approval if it has a clear business purpose and is not lavish or frequent. Entertainment above $250 per person requires pre-approval from the employee's manager and Compliance. Entertainment where the vendor does not attend is treated as a gift. Travel and accommodation paid by a vendor are prohibited unless pre-approved by Compliance.

title: Gifts, Entertainment and Vendor Conflicts of Interest Policy
text:
Gifts, Entertainment and Vendor Conflicts of Interest Policy (GIFT-POL, Current)
Section: Blackout during sourcing

**Blackout during sourcing.** Employees involved in an active RFP or sole-source evaluation (PRC-POL) may not accept any gift or entertainment, of any value, from any bidder until the contract is awarded. The blackout also applies during contract renewal negotiations (RNW-PRC).

title: Gifts, Entertainment and Vendor Conflicts of Interest Policy
text:
Gifts, Entertainment and Vendor Conflicts of Interest Policy (GIFT-POL, Current)
Section: Register

**Register.** Every gift or entertainment offered by a vendor and valued above $50, whether accepted or declined, must be recorded in the Gifts and Entertainment Register within 5 business days. Register entries are retained under RET-SCH.

title: Gifts, Entertainment and Vendor Conflicts of Interest Policy
text:
Gifts, Entertainment and Vendor Conflicts of Interest Policy (GIFT-POL, Current)
Section: Giving to vendors

**Giving to vendors.** Gifts and entertainment given by Northwind employees to vendor personnel follow the same value limits and must be recorded in the register.

title: Gifts, Entertainment and Vendor Conflicts of Interest Policy
text:
Gifts, Entertainment and Vendor Conflicts of Interest Policy (GIFT-POL, Current)
Section: Conflicts of interest

**Conflicts of interest.** A conflict exists where an employee, or a close family member or household member, has a financial interest in a vendor, is employed by a vendor, or has a close personal relationship with a vendor's owner or account team. Employees must disclose a conflict to Compliance as soon as they become aware of it and before taking part in any decision involving that vendor.

title: Gifts, Entertainment and Vendor Conflicts of Interest Policy
text:
Gifts, Entertainment and Vendor Conflicts of Interest Policy (GIFT-POL, Current)
Section: Recusal

**Recusal.** An employee with a disclosed conflict must recuse from vendor selection, evaluation, contract negotiation, performance rating, invoice approval, and exception approval for that vendor. RFP evaluators sign a conflict declaration before reviewing bids (PRC-POL §7.2).

title: Gifts, Entertainment and Vendor Conflicts of Interest Policy
text:
Gifts, Entertainment and Vendor Conflicts of Interest Policy (GIFT-POL, Current)
Section: Annual attestation

**Annual attestation.** All employees with vendor-facing responsibilities, including every Vendor Manager and Business Owner, complete an annual conflicts-of-interest attestation by January 31 each year.

title: Gifts, Entertainment and Vendor Conflicts of Interest Policy
text:
Gifts, Entertainment and Vendor Conflicts of Interest Policy (GIFT-POL, Current)
Section: Former employees

**Former employees.** A Northwind employee who leaves to join a vendor may not represent that vendor to Northwind for 12 months on any matter they handled while employed at Northwind.

title: Gifts, Entertainment and Vendor Conflicts of Interest Policy
text:
Gifts, Entertainment and Vendor Conflicts of Interest Policy (GIFT-POL, Current)
Section: Breaches

**Breaches.** Failure to disclose a conflict or to record a gift is a disciplinary matter. Where a breach affected a sourcing decision, Compliance may require the sourcing to be re-run.

title: Vendor Incident Notification SLA Schedule
text:
Vendor Incident Notification SLA Schedule (INCN-SLA, Current)
Section: 1. Purpose and Use

## 1. Purpose and Use

This schedule sets the maximum time a vendor has to notify Northwind of an incident. It is incorporated by reference into every vendor contract and every DPA (DPA-REQ clause 6). Legal must not agree longer deadlines without an approved exception under EXC-PRC. Shorter deadlines are always acceptable.

The clock starts when the vendor, or any of its subcontractors (FRTH-POL §7), becomes aware of the incident, not when its investigation concludes.

title: Vendor Incident Notification SLA Schedule
text:
Vendor Incident Notification SLA Schedule (INCN-SLA, Current)
Section: 2. Notification Deadlines

## 2. Notification Deadlines

| Incident type | Tier 1 | Tier 2 | Tier 3 | Tier 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Outage of a service supporting a critical business service | 1 hour | 4 hours | Next business day | Not applicable |
| Ransomware or destructive malware on systems that store or process Northwind data | 4 hours | 8 hours | 24 hours | 48 hours |
| Confirmed personal-data breach involving Northwind data | 24 hours | 48 hours | 72 hours | 72 hours |
| Unauthorized access to Northwind data, not yet confirmed as a breach | 24 hours | 48 hours | 72 hours | 72 hours |
| Incident at a material subcontractor affecting Northwind data or services | 24 hours | 48 hours | 72 hours | Not applicable |
| Harmful or materially incorrect output from an AI service used by Northwind (AIV-STD) | 72 hours | 72 hours | 72 hours | 72 hours |
| Regulatory inquiry or enforcement action concerning the contracted services | 5 business days | 5 business days | 10 business days | Not applicable |
| Change of control, or financial distress event (FIN-STD §5) | 10 business days | 10 business days | 30 days | Not applicable |

"Hours" are clock hours, including weekends and public holidays.

title: Vendor Incident Notification SLA Schedule
text:
Vendor Incident Notification SLA Schedule (INCN-SLA, Current)
Section: 3. Notification Content

## 3. Notification Content

The initial notification must include, to the extent known: a description of the incident; the time it occurred and the time it was discovered; the Northwind data and services affected; the containment actions taken; and a named vendor contact available around the clock. Missing information must not delay the initial notification.

title: Vendor Incident Notification SLA Schedule
text:
Vendor Incident Notification SLA Schedule (INCN-SLA, Current)
Section: 4. Follow-Up Reporting

## 4. Follow-Up Reporting

| Report | Deadline |
|---|---|
| Status updates during an active Tier 1 incident | Every 4 hours, or as agreed with the CISO office |
| Status updates during an active Tier 2 incident | Every 24 hours |
| Written root-cause analysis | 10 business days after containment |
| Remediation plan for root-cause findings | 20 business days after containment |

title: Vendor Incident Notification SLA Schedule
text:
Vendor Incident Notification SLA Schedule (INCN-SLA, Current)

## 5. Notification Channels

Vendors notify through both channels:

- the vendor incident mailbox, vendor-incidents@northwindcg.example, and
- the TPRM Office incident hotline, staffed around the clock.

For Tier 1 outages, the vendor must also call the named Northwind service owner. Notification to a Vendor Manager's personal mailbox alone does not satisfy this schedule.

title: Vendor Incident Notification SLA Schedule

Vendor Incident Notification SLA Schedule (INCN-SLA, Current)

The CISO office opens a third-party incident record within 1 hour of receiving a Tier 1 or Tier 2 notification. This procedure takes a vendor from approved sourcing decision to an active record in the vendor master. It applies after Procurement has completed sourcing under PRC-POL. No vendor may receive Northwind data, system access, or payment until Step 7 is complete (TPR-POL §4.3).

title: Vendor Onboarding Procedure
text:

Section: Step 1: Intake

## Step 1: Intake

The Business Owner submits a Vendor Intake Request in ProcureNet. The request must state the business need, estimated annual spend, the data classifications the vendor will access, the business service supported, and whether the vendor will use subcontractors. Incomplete requests are returned within 2 business days.

title: Vendor Onboarding Procedure

title: Vendor Onboarding Procedure
text:
Vendor Onboarding Procedure (ONB-PRC, Current)
Section: Step 3: Screening

Procurement initiates sanctions and adverse media screening under SANC-PRC. Screening must return clear, or any potential match must be adjudicated, before diligence evidence is requested from the vendor. This prevents Northwind from sharing its questionnaires with a sanctioned party.

title: Vendor Onboarding Procedure
text:

The TPRM Office coordinates the assessments required by DUE-STD. The vendor receives a single consolidated evidence request. Vendors have 15 business days to return evidence; one extension of 10 business days may be granted by the TPRM Office.

title: Vendor Onboarding Procedure
text:

Legal negotiates the contract using the clause library for the vendor's tier. Where personal data is involved, a DPA meeting DPA-REQ must be executed with or before the main agreement. Tier 1 and Tier 2 contracts must include an exit plan schedule (EXIT-PLN) and a right-to-audit clause (AUDT-GDE).

title: Vendor Onboarding Procedure

Procurement creates the vendor master record only after the TPRM Office records final approval in ProcureNet. The Vendor Manager is named on the record at activation. Access requests for vendor personnel may then be raised under ACC-STD.

title: Vendor Performance Monitoring Standard
text:
Vendor Performance Monitoring Standard (PERF-STD, Current)
Section: Section 1 — Purpose

## Section 1 — Purpose

Due diligence tells us whether a vendor can deliver. Performance monitoring tells us whether it does. This standard sets how Vendor Managers track service levels, run business reviews, and act when performance slips.

Vendor Performance Monitoring Standard (PERF-STD, Current)

title: Vendor Performance Monitoring Standard

text:
Vendor Performance Monitoring Standard (PERF-STD, Current)
Section: Section 4 — KPIs

## Section 4 — KPIs

Contracts for Tier 1 and Tier 2 vendors must define measurable KPIs with target and threshold values. At minimum: service availability, incident response time, defect or error rate, and, for operations outsourcing, processing accuracy. KPIs are reported by the vendor monthly, with supporting data Northwind can verify.

title: Vendor Performance Monitoring Standard
text:
Vendor Performance Monitoring Standard (PERF-STD, Current)
Section: Section 5 — Underperformance

## Section 5 — Underperformance

5.1 Any SLA breach is logged in ProcureNet with the service credit, if any, claimed.

5.2 A Red overall rating, or an SLA breach in two consecutive quarters, requires a performance improvement plan (PIP). The PIP sets specific actions, owners, and a remediation period of no more than 90 days.

5.3 If the PIP fails, the Vendor Manager escalates to the Business Owner and the TPRM Office, who decide whether to invoke contractual remedies or the exit plan (EXIT-PLN).

5.4 Service credits must be claimed. Waiving a service credit requires Business Owner approval recorded in ProcureNet.

title: Vendor Performance Monitoring Standard
text:
Vendor Performance Monitoring Standard (PERF-STD, Current)

## Section 6 — Inputs to Other Processes

The last four scorecards feed the renewal risk review (RNW-PRC Section 3). Red ratings for Tier 1 vendors are reported to the TPRC monthly. Scorecards and QBR minutes are retained under RET-SCH.

title: Vendor Performance Monitoring Standard
text:
Vendor Performance Monitoring Standard (PERF-STD, Current)

title: Vendor Risk Tiering Matrix
text:
Vendor Risk Tiering Matrix (TIER-MTX, Current)
Section: Section 1 — Purpose

## Section 1 — Purpose

The tier drives everything downstream: diligence depth, contract clauses, reassessment frequency, incident deadlines, and continuity targets. The TPRM Office assigns the tier at intake (TPR-POL §4.1) and confirms it after due diligence. A vendor takes the highest tier triggered by any single criterion.

title: Vendor Risk Tiering Matrix
text:

| Criterion | Tier 1 (Critical) | Tier 2 (High) | Tier 3 (Moderate) | Tier 4 (Low) |

| Service criticality | Supports a critical business service | Supports an important business service | Supports a non-critical internal function | Commodity goods or services |
| Annual spend | More than $1,000,000 | $250,000 to $1,000,000 | $50,000 to $249,999 | Under $50,000 |
